 Judgment
This appeal is filed by the appellant/claimant in O.P (MV) No.1886 of 2001 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Ernakulam.
The respondents herein are the respondents before the Tribunal.

2. According to the appellant/claimant, on 01.03.2000, at about 3.30 p.m., while the appellant was pillion riding on a motorcycle bearing registration No.KL-7/Y-4762, and when the vehicle reached the High School Junction, Edappally, due to the rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle by the first respondent, the vehicle skidded and as a result, the claimant sustained serious injuries.
The claimant approached the Tribunal claiming a total compensation of 1,50,000/-.
3. Before the Tribunal, the first and second respondents were the owner-cum-driver and the insurer of the offending vehicle respectively,

The second respondent insurer filed a written 2025:KER:50376 MACA NO. 1073 OF 2014 statement contending that the pillion rider was not covered by the policy and hence there was no liability to indemnify the insurer.

Before the Tribunal,
Exts.A1 to A8 and B1 were marked.
PW1 was examined.

The Tribunal, after analysing the pleadings and materials on record, exonerated the insurer from the liability and awarded a sum of 1,15,161/-
as compensation under different heads with interest @ 7% per annum from the date of petition till realization with proportionate costs from the first respondent - the owner of the vehicle.
Challenging the award exonerating the insurer as well as seeking enhancement of compensation, the claimant has come up in appeal.
4. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant and the learned Standing Counsel for the respondent insurer.

5. The learned counsel for the appellant claims enhancement mainly under the following heads:-

sentences.text: Notional Income
The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the injured was working as a distributor of foreign liquor.
He relied on Ext.A7 employment certificate, wherein the salary of the appellant was shown as 3,000/-.
However, the Tribunal had fixed the monthly income at 2,000/-.

The learned counsel further submits that even going by the judgment in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co.
Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the monthly income of a coolie is fixed at 2,500, for an accident of the year 2000.

entities.text:
Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co.
Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering Ext.A7 and also considering the fact that the claimant was working as a distributor of foreign liquor
, I find that the income claimed is to be accepted.
Accordingly, I find it appropriate to re-fix the notional monthly income at 3,000/- (Rupees Three Thousand Only).

II. Loss of earnings The learned counsel for the appellant submits that the Tribunal has taken only a period of three months for awarding 2025:KER:50376 MACA NO. 1073 OF 2014 compensation under the head loss of earnings.

Following are the injuries sustained by the appellant:
i) Abrasion on right elbow ii) Contusion on right knee iii) Fractures of right patella lateral condyle of right tibia and of right tibial spine
Considering the nature of injuries sustained by the appellant, I find that a period of five months can be taken for awarding compensation under the said head would be just and reasonable.

Since the notional monthly income has been re-fixed at 3,000/-, the total compensation payable under the said head would be 15,000/-
(3,000 x 5).
The Tribunal had granted an amount of 6,000/- under the said head.

Thus there will be an additional amount of 9,000/- (Rupees Nine Thousand Only)
under the said head.
2025:KER:50376 MACA NO. 1073 OF 2014 III.
Pain and suffering:
The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the Tribunal had granted only an amount of 12,000/- under the afore head.
Considering the age and nature of injuries sustained by the appellant, I find it appropriate to enhance the total compensation payable under the afoe head at 15,000/-.
Thus, there will be an additional amount of 3,000/- (Rupees Three Thousand Only) under the said head.
IV. Loss of amenities in life On a perusal of the award, it is seen that an amount of 6,000/- was awarded by the Tribunal under the head loss of amenities, which is on the lower side.

Considering the fact that the appellant was only 43 years at the time of accident and considering the loss of enjoyment of life, I find it appropriate to grant an additional amount of 9,000/- (Rupees Nine Thousand Only) totalling it to 15,000/- under the afore head.

C.V. Nandakumar vs Jayaprakash on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121156619/
3 2025:KER:50376 MACA NO. 1073 OF 2014 V. Compensation for permanent disability

The learned standing counsel appearing for the insurance company submitted that the injured was aged 43 years at the time of accident and the Tribunal has also accepted the age as 43, but the multiplier adopted is "15" instead of "14.
On a perusal of the award, since the age of the injured was 43 years, I find that the multiplier to be adopted is "14".

I find that the Tribunal has rightly adopted the multiplier,
following the judgment in National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi [2017 (4) KLT 662(SC).

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Since the notional income has been fixed at 3,000/-, the total compensation payable under the afore head is recalculated thus:
95,760/- (3,000 x 12 x 14 x 19/100).
The Tribunal had already awarded an amount of 68,400.
Thus there will be an additional amount of 27,360/- (Rupees Twenty Seven Thousand Three Hundred and Sixty Only) under the afore head.

6. The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the Tribunal had exonerated the insurance company from liability on 2025:KER:50376 MACA NO. 1073 OF 2014 the ground that the injured was a pillion rider and no additional premium had been paid to cover the risk of the pillion rider as per Ext.B1 policy.

However, upon calling for the trial court records and on a perusal of Ext.B1 policy,
both sides admit that the policy was a comprehensive policy and not an 'act only policy'.

Therefore,
the insurance company is liable to indemnify the owner and is liable to pay the compensation amount to the claimant.
Accordingly, I find that the finding of the Tribunal exonerating the insurance company from the liability and directing the owner to pay the award amount is liable to be set aside.
The insurance company, having issued the comprehensive policy, is liable to compensate for the injuries sustained to the pillion rider.

7. Though the appellant claimed enhancement of compensation under other heads, on a perusal of the records available, I am not inclined to interfere with the compensation 2025:KER:50376 MACA NO. 1073 OF 2014 awarded by the Tribunal under other heads since it appears to be just and reasonable.

8. Thus, the impugned award of the Tribunal is modified as follows:

Pain and sufferings 12,000 3,000 15000  Loss of amenities 6 and happiness in 6,000 9,000 15,000  life 7 Compensation 68,400 27,360 95,760  towards disability
Total amount  1,50,000 1,15,161 48,360 1,63,521  2025:KER:50376 MACA NO. 1073 OF 2014 Accordingly, this appeal is allowed.
The finding of the Tribunal exonerating the insurance company from the liability and directing the owner to pay the award amount is hereby set aside.

The appellant/claimant is awarded an additional compensation of 48,360/- (Rupees Forty Eight Thousand Three Hundred and Sixty Only) over and above the compensation awarded by the Tribunal with interest @ 7% per annum from the date of petition till realization with proportionate cost.

The respondent insurer shall deposit the award amount passed by the Tribunal and the enhanced amount together with interest and costs within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.

The claimant shall furnish copies of the PAN Card,
AADHAAR Card and Bank details before the respondent insurer within a period of one month so as to enable the insurance company to make the deposit as ordered above.
In case of failure to furnish details as above, it shall be open for the insurance company to deposit the said amount before the Tribunal.
Upon 2025:KER:50376 MACA NO. 1073 OF 2014 such deposit being made, the entire amount shall be disbursed to the appellant at the earliest, in accordance with law.
However, it is made clear that the enhanced compensation will not carry interest for the period of delay of 2219 days in filing the appeal.
